cues.en: Hey, it's Andrew Huang. Just a little bit of context for this video. It is a complete walkthrough of the basics of music theory in half an hour. Also sprinkled throughout are some exercises that you can do that will help you internalize these concepts because once they're in here, once they're natural to how you operate, it's like a superpower. You'll be able to come up with more ideas. You'll be able to work faster. The things that are in your head, you'll just be able to...
cues.zh: 大家好，我是 Andrew Huang。给这支视频做个简短的背景介绍。这是一份半小时的乐理基础完整实操指南。其中还穿插了一些练习，能帮你内化这些概念，因为一旦你掌握了它们，让它们融入你的创作直觉，那就跟拥有超能力一样。你能迸发出更多灵感。你的工作效率会更高。你脑海中的奇思妙想，就能直接...

cues.en: Do? It's magic. I love music theory. I'm a huge nerd. I actually made this video as a piece of bonus content for my online class, which you can find out more about at learnmonthly.com slash Andrew. I just wanted to have this there so that all the students would have the same foundation before heading into the rest of the course, which is much more about music production and songwriting and mixing and that kind of thing. But when I finished putting this lesson together, it really felt like a great thing to just share for free on YouTube, a crash course on music theory. So I hope it's helpful.
cues.zh: 变现？这简直是魔法。我超爱乐理。我就是个狂热的极客。其实我制作这个视频是作为我网课的额外福利内容，你可以通过 learnmonthly.com 斜杠 Andrew 了解更多信息。我只是想把它放在那里，好让所有学生在进入课程的其余部分之前都有相同的基础，后面的课程更多是关于音乐制作、词曲创作、混音以及诸如此类的内容。但当我把这节课整理完后，真的觉得把它作为一份免费的乐理速成课分享到 YouTube 上是个极好的主意。所以我希望它能派上用场。

cues.en: for you and if you're interested in a 20 lesson course about my whole approach to music making, more info about that at learnmonthly.com slash Andrew. Here's the theory lesson.
cues.zh: 对你有所帮助，如果你对涵盖我整个音乐创作方法的 20 课时课程感兴趣，可以在 learnmonthly.com 斜杠 Andrew 获取更多信息。下面是乐理课。

cues.en: So what is music theory? It's essentially the language behind music. It gives you the tools you need to understand and interpret and communicate about music. Everyone in this class is mastered talking. Whatever your home language is, it's second nature to you now. You can use it without thinking about it, and it's an incredibly powerful way to interpret the world around you and communicate with other people, relate to them, express yourself. Music theory does the same thing for music. It'll help you understand how chords and notes and rhythms and melodies all work together, and as you get good at the language,
cues.zh: 那么什么是乐理？它本质上是音乐背后的语言。它为你提供理解、诠释和交流音乐所需的工具。班上的每个人都已经精通说话了。无论你的母语是什么，现在它对你来说都是第二天性。你可以不假思索地使用它，这是一种无比强大的方式，能让你诠释周围的世界，与他人沟通、产生共鸣并表达自我。乐理对音乐的作用也是一样的。它能帮你理解和弦、音符、节奏和旋律是如何协同工作的，随着你对这门语言越来越熟练，

cues.en: you're able to use it really effectively without thinking about it. I hear from a lot of people that they get stuck in this place with music theory where it feels like it's just work and it's really cerebral and it's all about what key am I in and what chord is this and what scale should I be using and I really want to stress that there is a place beyond that where if you use it enough it becomes as natural and fluid as talking. I know that when you're talking you're not thinking about do I use past tense or present tense or like
cues.zh: 你就能真正高效地使用它，甚至不需要去思考。我听很多人说，他们在乐理上遇到了瓶颈，觉得这只是一项苦差事，而且过于烧脑，满脑子都是我在什么调、这是什么和弦、我该用哪个音阶，我真的想强调的是，在这之上还有一个境界，只要你用得足够多，它就会变得像说话一样自然流畅。我知道你在说话时，根本不会去想我是该用过去时还是现在时，或者诸如此类的事情

cues.en: What is the word for this very common item that I use every day? You're a natural at it. You just look at this and your brain goes, ah.
cues.zh: 这个非常常见的东西，我每天都在用，它叫什么？你天生就会。你一看它，大脑马上就说，啊。

cues.en: It's a cat. With enough experience, you can absolutely get to that same level of natural automatic use of music theory. Similarly, with language, sometimes we come across a word or a concept that we don't know, but we can learn it if it's explained to us using the words and the concepts that we already do understand. In music, if I come across something really advanced that I don't understand, it's the music theory fundamentals that allow me to figure it out and learn it and add it to my arsenal. So we're going to start right at the beginning and talk about notes. What is...
cues.zh: 是猫。只要经验足够，你完全能达到同样自然、自动运用乐理的水平。同样，在语言中，有时我们会遇到不认识的词或概念，但只要用我们已经理解的词和概念来解释，我们就能学会。在音乐中，如果我遇到某个非常高级、我不理解的东西，正是乐理基础让我能弄懂它、学会它，并把它加入我的武器库。所以我们要从头开始，讲讲音符。什么是……

cues.en: Well, sound is made up of vibrations and our ears and brains are really good at interpreting those vibrations. When the vibrations are faster, we hear them as being higher, and when the vibrations are slower, we hear them as being lower. If the vibrations happen at a consistent rate, then we perceive them as having a consistent pitch or frequency or a note. So for example, if I play this guitar string...
cues.zh: 声音由振动构成，我们的耳朵和大脑非常擅长解读这些振动。振动越快，我们听到的音就越高；振动越慢，我们听到的音就越低。如果振动以稳定的速率发生，我们就会感知到稳定的音高、频率或音符。比如，如果我拨动这根吉他弦……

cues.en: It's vibrating, it's physically moving back and forth, in this case 110 times per second, and that's quickly traveling through the air and reaching our ears, and we perceive that as the note, A.
cues.zh: 它在振动，在物理上前后运动，在这个例子里是每秒110次，然后迅速通过空气传到我们耳朵里，我们把它感知为音符A。

cues.en: Now in case you aren't aware, the vast majority of popular music is made using only 12 notes. Almost all the music you've ever heard is made up of these 12 notes and how they relate to each other because as a culture we've discovered that that generally sounds better than frequencies that don't relate together in that way. And there are actually mathematical ratios that explain why all those relationships sound good together, but for the purposes of this course we don't need to get into that. We've given the notes names so it's easy to refer to them and the names relate to the layout of a piano keyboard.
cues.zh: 你可能不知道，绝大多数流行音乐都只用 12 个音写成。你听过的几乎所有音乐，都是由这 12 个音以及它们之间的相互关系构成的，因为作为一种文化，我们发现这通常比那些不以这种方式相互关联的频率听起来更好。其实有数学比例可以解释为什么这些关系组合起来很好听，但就本课程而言，我们不需要深入讲这个。我们给这些音起了名字，方便指代，而这些名字与钢琴键盘的布局有关。

cues.en: So the white notes are named A through G. The black keys are named relative to the white keys with the words sharp and flat. Sharp means higher and flat means lower. So for example, with this note, it's above an F. So it's an F sharp. But it's also below this G. So in some situations, you'd call it a G flat. As you can see, there are a lot more than just 12 keys on this keyboard, but the same notes actually repeat themselves higher and lower.
cues.zh: 所以白键上的音命名为 A 到 G。黑键的音是相对于白键来命名的，用“升”和“降”这两个词。升表示更高，降表示更低。比如这个音，它在 F 上方，所以是升 F。但它也在 G 下方，所以在某些情况下，你会叫它降 G。如你所见，这个键盘上远不止 12 个键，但相同的音其实会在更高和更低处重复。

cues.en: That's the one mathematical ratio that I'll get into here and it's actually kind of fascinating But our brains can tell when a vibration is twice as fast as another one It sounds like the same note if I play an A here and an A here
cues.zh: 这是我这里唯一要讲的数学比例，其实还挺有意思的。我们的大脑能分辨出一个振动比另一个快一倍；如果我在这儿弹一个 A，再在这儿弹一个 A，听起来就像同一个音。

cues.en: It's the same, but one's higher and one's lower. It's crazy. And by the way, this distance of going 12 notes up or down to the next identically named note is called an octave. The increment between each individual note is called a semitone or a half step, and the increment between two half steps is called a whole step or a whole tone or a tone.
cues.zh: 它是同一个音，只是一个更高、一个更低。太神奇了。顺便说，向上或向下走 12 个音到下一个同名音，这段距离叫八度。每个单独音之间的间隔叫半音（semitone，也叫 half step），两个半音之间的间隔叫全音（whole step、whole tone 或 tone）。

cues.en: So music is then built on the relationships between these notes, and there are common combinations of notes that we call a key, not to be confused with the word key when we're referring to a piano key. A key is sort of like a guide of what notes will sound good together in a piece of music, and most pieces of music use only one key. If you remember when I said most songs don't even use all 12 notes, most commonly they would use seven, and that's because there are seven notes in major and minor keys which are the most common keys. So let's look at an example of a key.
cues.zh: 所以音乐就是建立在这些音符之间的关系之上，音符有一些常见的组合我们称之为调（key），不要把它和我们指钢琴琴键（key）时的那个词混淆。调有点像是一首乐曲中哪些音符听起来很搭的指南，而且大多数乐曲只使用一个调。如果你还记得我之前说过，大多数歌曲甚至不会用到全部12个音符，最常见的是用7个，那是因为在大调和小调这两个最常见的调中正好有7个音符。所以我们来看一个调的例子。

cues.en: The easiest one is C major because it uses all the white notes.
cues.zh: 最简单的就是C大调，因为它只用白键。

cues.en: So when I play the notes out like that, that's called the C major scale. And the words scale and key are often used interchangeably, but for your knowledge, a key is more like the home base group of notes that a song is based on, and a scale is a set of notes that you would play in conjunction with that. So a lot of times you're playing the exact scale that matches the key that you're in, but sometimes depending on the flavor that you want or the genre that you're working with, you'll use a different scale over your home key. So for example, a lot of blues music is written in
cues.zh: 所以当我把这些音符弹出来时，这就叫做C大调音阶。scale（音阶）和key（调）这两个词经常混用，但为了让你有所了解，调更像是歌曲所基于的大本营音符组，而音阶则是你会配合弹奏的一组音符。所以很多时候你弹奏的正是与你所在的主调相匹配的音阶，但有时根据你想要的风格或你所处理的流派，你会在主调上使用不同的音阶。例如，很多布鲁斯音乐都是用

cues.en: major because that's like the standard tuning of the guitar but blues solos typically happen with the E blues scale or E pentatonic minor scale. Those scales have some of the same notes as E major but some that are different and that's what imparts the bluesy flavor. But let's look at the C major scale again and the relationships between the notes. So if we're in the key of C we call C the root note and that's the note that we start the scale on. Notice that as we go up the scale the notes have a spacing of whole
cues.zh: 大调写的，因为这就像吉他的标准调音，但布鲁斯独奏通常会使用E布鲁斯音阶或E五声音阶小调。这些音阶包含一些与E大调相同的音符，但也有一些不同，这正是布鲁斯风味来源所在。不过我们再来看看C大调音阶以及音符之间的关系。所以如果我们处于C大调，我们称C为根音（root note），也就是我们开始弹奏音阶的那个音符。请注意，当我们顺着音阶往上时，音符之间的间距是全音、

cues.en: whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. Starting here you go up two, up two, up one, up two, up two, up two, and up one. Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
cues.zh: 全音、半音、全音、全音、全音、半音。从这里开始，升两个半音、升两个半音、升一个半音、升两个半音、升两个半音、升两个半音，再升一个半音。全音、全音、半音、全音、全音、全音、半音。

cues.en: that is the formula of a major scale. So if your song is in C major, you'll know that these are the notes that you'll mostly or maybe exclusively use because they'll sound better than the notes that aren't in C major. It's also common practice and really helpful to number the notes of the scale, starting with one at the root. So if C is our one, then D would be our two, or the second degree, or just the second. E would be the three, or the third degree, or the third, and so on.
cues.zh: 这就是大调音阶的公式。所以如果你的歌是 C 大调，你就会知道这些是你主要、或者可能只会用到的音，因为它们比 C 大调之外的音听起来更合适。给音阶中的音编号也是常见做法，而且很有帮助，从根音开始编号为 1。所以如果 C 是 1，那么 D 就是 2，也就是第二级，或者直接叫第二个音。E 就是 3，也就是第三级，或者第三个音，以此类推。

cues.en: Practice applying the major scale formula to a few different notes. Remember that the spacing between the notes in the major scale is whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. So for example, if you picked A major, you would start on A, and you would move up a whole tone, so skip one and then play the next. That's B, then another whole tone, skip one, play the next, that's C sharp, then just a half tone, D, another whole tone, skip one, play the E, another whole tone, skip the F, play the F sharp,
cues.zh: 练习把大调音阶公式套用到几个不同的音上。记住，大调音阶中音与音之间的间隔是全、全、半、全、全、全、半。比如你选 A 大调，就从 A 开始，向上走一个全音，也就是隔一个音，弹下一个音。那是 B；再走一个全音，隔一个音，弹下一个音，那是 C sharp；然后只走一个半音，到 D；再一个全音，隔一个音，弹 E；再一个全音，跳过 F，弹 F sharp，

cues.en: another whole tone, skip the G, play the G sharp, and then finally another half tone to get back up to A. Also practice identifying the notes, both using the absolute letter names that go with them, as well as the numbered scale degrees that go with each key that you're in. In a major scale, each letter name appears exactly once, no matter how many accidentals there are. Accidentals meaning a sharp or a flat. So to name the notes in an A major scale, we would start on A and go up alphabetically from there.
cues.zh: 再走一个全音，跳过 G，弹 G sharp；最后再走一个半音，回到 A。还要练习识别这些音，既用它们对应的绝对字母名，也用你当前所在调对应的音阶级数编号。在大调音阶中，每个字母名都恰好出现一次，不管有多少变音记号。变音记号指的是升号或降号。所以要说出 A 大调音阶中的音，我们会从 A 开始，然后按字母顺序往上数。

cues.en: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and of course G is the last letter that we use in music, so we wrap back around to an A over here. But we also have to add sharp to the names of the black keys. C sharp, F sharp, and G sharp. So it's A, B, C sharp, D, E, F sharp, G sharp, A.
cues.zh: A、B、C、D、E、F、G，当然 G 是我们在音乐中使用的最后一个字母，所以我们在这里回到了 A。但我们还得给黑键加上升音符号（#）。C#、F# 和 G#。所以它是 A、B、C#、D、E、F#、G#、A。

cues.en: So even though these notes are C sharp, F sharp, and G sharp, because they're a half step above C, F, and G, they're also a half step below D, G, and A. So you could call them D flat, G flat, and A flat. In A major, we use the sharp names for these notes. That way, each letter name appears exactly once in the scale, and it makes it easier to remember and communicate about these notes. As opposed to if we use the flat names, and then the scale was A, B, D flat, D, E, G flat, A flat,
cues.zh: 所以即使这些音符是 C#、F# 和 G#，因为它们比 C、F 和 G 高半音，所以它们也比 D、G 和 A 低半音。所以你也可以叫它们 D♭、G♭ 和 A♭。在 A 大调中，我们对这些音符使用升音名称。这样，每个字母名称在音阶中正好出现一次，这使得记忆和交流这些音符变得更容易。与使用降音名称相反，那样的话音阶就是 A、B、D♭、D、E、G♭、A♭、

cues.en: A, where you have skips between the letters and some of them repeat twice. So to name the notes in the major scale, you start at the root note and go up alphabetically, and that's how you know whether to name the black keys as sharps or flats. In a couple of special cases, you might even name white keys sharp or flat. For instance, if you wrote an A sharp major, your second note, a whole tone up would be this, which is a C, but in A sharp major, we would call it a B sharp.
cues.zh: A，此时字母之间会出现跳跃，其中一些会重复两次。因此，要为大调音阶中的音符命名，你从根音开始，按字母顺序往上数，这就是你如何判断是将黑键命名为升音还是降音的方法。在少数特殊情况下，你甚至可能会将白键命名为升音或降音。例如，如果你写一个 A# 大调，你的第二个音符——往上一个全音——就会是这个，也就是 C，但在 A# 大调中，我们会把它叫做 B#。

cues.en: Because of this, though, a lot of people prefer to refer to this key as B flat, which reduces the confusion of needing to use a sharp name on a white key. I know this is a lot of information, so don't worry if it takes you a little bit to get the hang of it, but that's also exactly why practice is important. Naming the scale degrees is much easier, obviously. The root note you picked is the first degree, and then you just count up for each consecutive note in the scale. So in A major, A is the first degree, B is the second, C sharp is the third, D is the fourth, E is the fifth,
cues.zh: 正因如此，很多人更喜欢把这个调称为 B♭，这减少了在白键上使用升音名称所带来的困惑。我知道这是大量的信息，所以如果你需要花点时间才能掌握它，也不用担心，这也是练习之所以重要的原因。显而易见，为音阶级数命名要简单得多。你选择的根音是第一级，然后顺着音阶中的每个连续音符依次往上数即可。所以在 A 大调中，A 是第一级，B 是第二级，C# 是第三级，D 是第四级，E 是第五级，

cues.en: F sharp is the sixth and G sharp is the seventh. So the next big piece of the puzzle for working with notes and making music sound good is chords. Chords are just multiple notes played at the same time. They do most of the work of setting the emotion in the song and guide the listener through some kind of musical story. Since chords are made up of notes and notes are in keys, chords are almost always in the same key. If you randomly play a bunch of notes from C major, you're playing some kind of chord from C major.
cues.zh: F# 是第六级，G# 是第七级。因此，处理音符和让音乐动听的下一个关键部分就是和弦。和弦就是同时弹奏多个音符。它们承担了为歌曲定下情感基调的大部分工作，并引导听众体验某种音乐故事。既然和弦由音符组成，而音符又在调性之中，那么和弦也几乎总是处于同一调性中。如果你随机弹奏 C 大调中的一堆音符，你就是在弹奏来自 C 大调的某种和弦。

cues.en: The most common chords contain three notes that have a very specific relationship to each other, and we call that the root, third, and fifth. So in C major, I can play the root, C, the third of C major, E, and the fifth of C major, G. And that gives us a C major chord. Root, third, fifth. You can think of this as playing a note from the scale, skipping a note from the scale.
cues.zh: 最常见的和弦包含三个彼此关系非常独特的音符，我们称之为根音、三音和五音。所以以C大调为例，我可以弹奏根音C、C大调的三音E，以及C大调的五音G。这样就构成了一个C大调和弦。根音、三音、五音。你可以这样理解：弹奏音阶中的一个音，跳过音阶中的一个音。

cues.en: playing a note from the scale, skipping a note from the scale, and then playing another note from the scale. This type of chord is also called a triad. Now we can take this triad shape and move the root so that it's any other note from C major, and we'll get another chord from C major. So since this chord starts on F, it's an F chord, but here's where we need to get a little fluid with our lingo, because the root of an F chord is F, the third is A, and the fifth is C.
cues.zh: 弹奏音阶中的一个音，跳过音阶中的一个音，然后再弹奏音阶中的另一个音。这种类型的和弦也叫做三和弦。现在我们可以保持这个三和弦的形状并移动根音，使其成为C大调中的任意其他音符，这样就能得到C大调中的另一个和弦。所以因为这个和弦从F开始，它就是一个F和弦，但这就是我们需要灵活运用术语的地方，因为F和弦的根音是F，三音是A，五音是C。

cues.en: But we're still in the key of C major where C is the root and F is the fourth in relation to C and A is the sixth in relation to C. Don't worry if this is confusing right now, it's the kind of thing you get the hang of the more you use it but it's definitely helpful to get used to the numbered relationships within chords as well as how they relate to the overall key. So there are two really common chord types in music and that's major and minor. People usually say major sounds happy and minor sounds sad.

Also try removing the fourth and seventh degrees from your major scale to make a major pentatonic scale, and then try playing melodies using that scale. cues.zh: 选一个调，在该调内做一个和弦进行，然后录进你的音乐软件。有了这个之后，试着在上面弹一些旋律，思考当前和弦里有哪些音，也许还有一些和弦外音，但能解决到和弦内的音。还可以试着从大调音阶中去掉第四级和第七级，做成大调五声音阶，然后用这个音阶弹旋律。你可能会发现，这样更容易弹出好听的东西。

cues.en: For a quick example of finding a major pentatonic scale, why don't we look at the key of F. The notes there are F, G, A, Bb, C, D, E. So if we number those, it's 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. Bb is the 4, E is the 7. We'll take that out of our scale, leaving us with F, G, A, C, D. That is the F major pentatonic scale. The last component of theory fundamentals is rhythm and how to count it.
cues.zh: 快速找个大调五声音阶的例子，我们来看看F调。那里的音是F、G、A、Bb、C、D、E。给它们编号就是1、2、3、4、5、6、7。Bb是第4级，E是第7级。把它们从音阶里去掉，剩下F、G、A、C、D。这就是F大调五声音阶。乐理基础的最后一个组成部分是节奏，以及如何数拍子。

cues.en: How do you tell when things are played, whether that's chords or melodies or drum beats? That's based on the musical counting system. Music is divided into equal sized portions called bars or measures. And typically in Western music, you'll have four beats to a measure, which we count. One, two, three.
cues.zh: 你怎么判断东西是在什么时候演奏的，不管是和弦、旋律还是鼓点？这靠的是音乐计数系统。音乐被分成等长的小段，叫小节。西方音乐里通常一小节有四拍，我们这样数：一、二、三。

cues.en: Four. So if one note is the length of a bar, we'd call it a whole note. If it's two beats, which is half of the bar, we'd call it a half note. And then each of those four notes that we were counting as beats in the bar are quarters of the bar. Those are quarter notes. So you can have sounds, instruments, whatever, playing on these beats or anywhere in between them. And if something is on the beat, then we would say it's on the one, for example. But if it's in between these beats, then we need to do what's called subdividing, which is like increasing the resol-
cues.zh: 四。所以如果一个音符的长度是一小节，我们就叫它全音符。如果它是两拍，也就是半小节，我们就叫它二分音符。而我们在小节里当作拍子数的那四个音符，每个都是小节的四分之一；这些就是四分音符。所以你可以在这些拍点上，或在它们之间的任何位置演奏声音、乐器等等。如果某个东西在拍点上，比如我们会说它落在“一”上。但如果它在这些拍之间，就要做所谓的细分，也就是提高我们计数的分辨

cues.en: of our counting. If we subdivide beats in half, we count it as one and two and three and four and, and those ands are exactly halfway in between each of those beats, so now that resolution is eighth notes. We can subdivide further, again getting exactly halfway in between our main beats and our ands, so that would be one E and a two E and a three E and a four E and a. So that puts us at 16th notes, and even though you can keep on subdividing forever, the main parts of songs are usually not played any faster than
cues.zh: 率。如果我们把一拍对半细分，就数成一 和 二 和 三 和 四 和，而那些“和”正好在每两拍的正中间，所以现在这个分辨率就是八分音符。我们还能继续细分，再次正好落在主拍和“和”的正中间，那就成了 一 E 和 a、二 E 和 a、三 E 和 a、四 E 和 a。这样我们就到了十六分音符，而且尽管可以一直细分下去，歌曲的主要部分通常不会演奏得比

cues.en: 16th notes. And this really is a pretty universal system in Western music. If you're talking to anybody who's had some music education and you say something is on the 2E, they'll probably know what you're talking about. So getting used to using this counting system will allow you to play music better because you'll be able to better feel where you are within the beats. It'll also allow you to interpret and decipher and remember different kinds of rhythmic material because it gives you a structure for those rhythms to live in. So let's say you're out and about and you get an idea or you hear something that you want to try.
cues.zh: 十六分音符更快。而且这在西方音乐里确实是个相当通用的系统。如果你跟任何受过一些音乐教育的人说某个东西在 2E 上，他们大概知道你在说什么。所以习惯使用这个计数系统能让你把音乐演奏得更好，因为你能更好地感受自己在拍子中的位置。它还能让你解读、辨清并记住不同种类的节奏素材，因为它给这些节奏提供了一个可以安放的结构。比如你在外面走动，突然有了一个想法，或者听到某样你想尝试的东西。
